function.name: observe
function.description: See the current game screen and the game state read from memory (location, party, map). Pending ordinary battle text advances to the next decision; all messages are listed. Pending ordinary field dialogue also advances to the next decision; all pages are listed.

function.name: press
function.description: Press Game Boy Advance buttons in order (up to 8), then see the resulting screen and game state. Direction-only field travel runs whenever native controls permit it; the harness, not the model, owns this choice. Field dialogue advances automatically: once a conversation opens, the harness presses B through every page until the next decision point and lists the pages; inputs left in your batch are not sent. Battle text advances the same way: while a battle runs its own messages, the harness presses B through each waiting message until a battle menu, a YES/NO question, another screen or the battle's end, and lists every battle message shown.

function.name: choose_evolution
function.description: Explicitly choose whether to evolve or cancel the current POKéMON evolution. The game waits for this decision at the native cancellation window. Neither option is recommended. Ordinary buttons cannot resolve this choice. Move-learning prompts afterward use their own controls. Refuses when no eligible evolution is waiting.

decision.description: evolve allows the current evolution to complete; cancel stops it.

function.name: navigate_to
function.description: Walks to a tile two or more tiles away; give the destination and it finds the route around walls, ledges, water and people. For a person, object, warp or map exit that the readout lists with a navigate_to_target target, use navigate_to_target with that target instead. Walk to a coordinate on the current map using A* over the whole current map. Supply its map_id. Walks the full route one ordinary button at a time, re-planning before every press; avoids unsupported terrain, hops a ledge only in its arrow direction, never crosses a walled side of a + tile, walks sand, cave and other floor the game allows, and never crosses a warp unless it is the destination. Stops on blocked or unexpected movement, locks, map changes, or when the route stops getting shorter. For a listed warp, it may choose a reachable equivalent warp with the same complete destination and known activation behavior; if already on a directional warp, it presses the required direction once and verifies the map changed. Does not press A. Inspect the returned state before continuing. It cannot walk while a message is open: dismiss the message with B first. To talk to a person, use an object, or go through a door, stairs, another warp or a map exit that the readout lists with a navigate_to_target target, call navigate_to_target with that target instead. Straight corridors of plain floor or tall grass use explicit strides of at most 8 tiles, validated against native movement before each step. Strides stop before turns, other grass, ledges, warps, objects, script coordinates and elevation changes; special steps walk without automatic running. Before it walks, it checks the planned route against the sight of every trainer on this map you have not beaten; when one can see a tile of the route it does not walk and names the trainer and the tile. Call it again with confirm_trainer_sight: true to walk that route anyway. Prefer routes avoiding matching coordinate scripts; when no such route exists, the first matching coordinate script is a walkable observation boundary: ordinary steps walk without automatic running, strides stop before script coordinates, and navigation returns the resulting state after a trigger entry attempt before any further movement. If it ends in dialogue or a battle, the text advances automatically to the next decision point and its pages are listed. Give because: {quote, rationale?}; quote contains only exact observed words. Optional rationale is your unverified explanation. Matching verifies words only, not speaker identity or destination.

confirm_trainer_sight.description: Only after navigate_to said a trainer you have not beaten can see a tile of this route: true walks the route anyway.

quote.description: Only the exact words copied from a game observation that make this destination the place to go. Do not add a speaker name or explanation. Line breaks, case and curly quotes are ignored.

rationale.description: Optional explanation in your own words. This is not checked or treated as observed evidence.

because.description: Required. Quote, word for word, what the game showed you that makes this the place to go: a person's words, the Story goal line, or a readout line that shows the destination on this map (a door, a person's position, an exit or a Map connections line). Copy it; do not paraphrase or add to it. An exit the readout says cannot be reached on foot from where you stand is not a reason to walk to it. Put only copied evidence in quote; rationale is optional and unverified.

function.name: navigate_to_target
function.description: The way to reach a person, object, door, stairs, other warp or walking map exit that the readout lists with a navigate_to_target target: it walks there, faces it and talks to it, uses it or goes through it, once. Pass the current map_id and the target exactly as the readout writes it after "navigate_to_target target". The harness chooses the reachable approach and continues progress-making route segments without an end-to-end command cap. Dialogue the activation opens is advanced for you as with navigate_to. It returns control immediately if a battle, a menu, a script, forced movement, a map transition or unavailable input interrupts travel, and says why when it refuses or stops early. For anything without a navigate_to_target target, use navigate_to. For a loaded NPC selected by object local_id, navigate_to_target follows its verified current position after each bounded movement action, then faces it and presses A once. This path returns after at most 32 movement, facing or activation attempts, including changed-state retries, or earlier if identity, field control or a supported route becomes unavailable. Before it walks, it checks the route it plans against the sight of every trainer on this map you have not beaten, except one you asked to talk to; when one can see a tile of the route it does not walk and names the trainer and the tile. Call it again with confirm_trainer_sight: true to walk that route anyway. Exception for an explicitly requested unloaded trainer listed in current-map trainer facts: navigate_to_target may approach its template tile, then returns without facing or pressing A. The template may have moved; inspect the current returned state before choosing an interaction. For a static scripted object template listed in current-map native facts, pass target kind static_object with its local_id. This approaches only: current presence and position are unverified, scripts may relocate it, and the tool returns without facing or pressing A even if the object has loaded. No automatic field or battle text is advanced. If it ends in dialogue or a battle, the text advances automatically to the next decision point and its pages are listed. Static template requests return immediately without automatic field or battle text advancement.

confirm_trainer_sight.description: Only after navigate_to_target said a trainer you have not beaten can see a tile of its route: true walks the route anyway.

function.name: explore_map
function.description: Deterministically chooses one reachable listed interaction not previously attempted by this explorer. When none remain, chooses a reachable walking connection. It navigates to and activates only that one target, returning immediately on battle, dialogue, menus, scripts, forced movement or map changes. If it ends in dialogue or a battle, the text advances automatically to the next decision point and its pages are listed.

function.name: battle_action
function.description: Choose a battle action in one call, only while a battle waits for your choice: action fight with move (a move name your active POKéMON knows), bag, pokemon or run. The harness reads the battle menu's cursor from the game's memory and presses the buttons one at a time (moving the highlight, then A), checking the cursor after each press; it stops and says why if anything is not as expected. It refuses without pressing when no battle is waiting for a choice, when the active POKéMON does not know the move, or when the move has no PP. bag and pokemon open the BAG or the POKéMON screen and stop there; choose the item or POKéMON with press. In a double battle the game asks for each of your POKéMON in turn: call battle_action once for each; the result names the POKéMON it chose for and the one asked next. A move that hits one chosen POKéMON needs target there, and the harness moves the target highlight the same checked way. YES/NO and Safari choices are not handled; use press. A refused call presses nothing and does not automatically advance text. When the returned state says a message is waiting for A or B, use press with A or B; battle_action cannot choose FIGHT there. While the game runs its own text or animation without a waiting input, wait and observe. Pending ordinary field dialogue advances first; the queued action is not executed, so choose again from the returned state. Before validating an action, pending ordinary battle text advances to a decision. Those automatic B presses are listed separately. If another choice or a bound is reached, the requested action is not executed. If the battle then runs its own text, the text advances automatically to the next decision point and its pages are listed.

action.description: fight, bag, pokemon or run: the battle menu option to choose.

move.description: With fight: the name of the move to use, as the battle shows it (for example EMBER).

target.description: With fight in a double battle: the POKéMON the move hits, by its name as the battle shows it, or foe left / foe right / ally / self (left and right as on the screen). Needed for a move that hits one chosen POKéMON; ignored otherwise.

function.name: learn_move
function.description: Answer the game's move-learning prompts in one call, only while one is open for the move being learned: "Delete a move to make room for …?", "Stop learning …?", the "… is trying to learn …" and "… can't learn more than four moves" pages before them, or the summary screen's list of moves to forget. forget is one of the four moves the POKéMON knows, as the game names it: the harness answers YES to deleting a move, moves the summary screen's highlight one step at a time to that move (checking the highlighted move after each press) and presses A. forget "none": it answers NO to deleting a move and YES to "Stop learning …?", so the POKéMON keeps the moves it knows. It then checks the party's moves and reports what the game printed. It refuses without pressing when no move-learning prompt is open or the move is not one of the four, and stops and says why if the screen changes unexpectedly. Neither choice is recommended. press still works on these prompts. When forget is "none", decline_move is required: name the offered move you intend to decline, as the game shows it. The harness checks the actual offered move after waiting and before every input; a different or unreadable offer stops the action and returns the current observation. Inspect it and make a fresh choice. A matching named decline remains allowed.

forget.description: The move to forget for the new move, by its name as the game lists it among the four moves the POKéMON knows (for example SCRATCH), or "none" to keep the four moves and not learn the new one.

decline_move.description: Required when forget is "none": the name of the offered move you are declining, as the game shows it. A mismatch refuses without declining.

function.name: get_dialogue
function.description: Search every dialogue page the harness advanced through this run, newest first, each whole with its speaker, map, position, turn and event number. Filters: speaker, contains (words), map (name or map id), last (default 10). It reads the record only; it does not press buttons.

speaker.description: Only pages whose speaker contains this text (case-insensitive), such as MOM or SCIENTIST_1.

map.description: Only pages shown on a map whose name or map id (for example 1/4) contains this text.

last.description: How many matching pages to return, newest first (default 10).

function.name: select_menu_option
function.description: Select one currently visible option in a verified vertical START or field multichoice menu, using checked UP/DOWN and one A press.
